title: 1976 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship
text:
{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland | year = 1976 | image = | dates = 2 May – 5 September 1976 | teams = 13 | connacht = | munster = Cork | leinster = Wexford | ulster = | matches = 13 | poty = [[Tony Doran]] | team = Cork | titles = 22nd | captain = [[Ray Cummins]] | manager = [[Bertie Troy]] | team2 = Wexford | captain2 = [[Tony Doran]] | manager2 = [[Tom Neville (hurler)|Tom Neville]] | totalgoals = | totalpoints = | topscorer = [[File: Colours of Wexford.svg|border|20px]] [[Mick Butler (Wexford hurler)|Mick Butler]] (3–20) | previous = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1975|1975]] | next = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1977|1977]] }} The '''1976 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 90th staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter county|inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament. The championship began on 2 May 1976 and ended on 5 September 1976. [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] were the [[1975 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]] but were defeated by [[Wexford GAA|Wexfoprd]] in the Leinster final.{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/1975-the-summer-the-west-was-stirred-from-its-slumber-206477.html|title=1975: The summer the West was stirred from its slumber|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=5 September 2012|date=24 May 2020|first=Enda|last=McEvoy}} On 5 September 1976, [[Cork GAA|Cork]] won the championship following a 2–21 to 4–11 defeat of Wexford in the [[1976 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]] at [[Croke Park]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/rebel-goalkeepers-behind-the-push-for-glory-1.997503|title=Rebel goalkeepers behind the push for glory|publisher=Irish Times|date=2 September 2006|access-date=24 May 2020|first=Ian|last=O'Riordan}} This was their 22nd All-Ireland title overall and their first title since [[1970 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1970]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/obrien-hails-corbetts-hat-trick-heroics-130516.html|title=O'Brien hails Corbett's hat-trick heroics|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=11 September 2011|access-date=12 March 2013|first=Simon|last=Lewis}} Wexford's [[Mick Butler (Wexford hurler)|Mick Butler]] was the championship's top scorer with 3–20.
